lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Make sure the code profile links directly to relevant work and is accessible.
items.because: Readers need to be able to inspect the work.

items.says: Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It is generally unnecessary for a resume and can expose you to irrelevant bias.

items.says: Remove nationality unless it directly clarifies work authorization or is requested.
items.because: Work eligibility should be communicated specifically and accurately.

items.says: Keep the expected M.S. graduation date current and unambiguous.
Consider adding GPA, honors, or relevant coursework to the education entries if strong and useful.
items.because: They should be useful for the roles being targeted.

items.says: Define what “diagnostic accuracy” means.
items.because: Without the metric, the 35% improvement is hard to interpret.

items.says: Specify the evaluation set and comparison baseline for the accuracy improvement.
items.because: Without the test setup, the major claim is hard to interpret.

items.says: Explain how reviewer disagreement was measured and compared.
Clarify your role in designing or implementing the routing.
Clarify what “in-scope signals” means.
items.because: The term is central to the result.

items.says: Explain the rollout setup and reward design for the GRPO result.
items.because: The paired improvements may otherwise invite scrutiny.

items.says: Clarify the baseline and measurement conditions, including how equal accuracy and latency were established.
items.because: The paired improvements may otherwise invite scrutiny.

items.says: State what you contributed to the evaluation harness.
Explain how the 14 checkpoints were evaluated.
Clarify what counted as an accuracy regression.
Clarify whether “before release” refers to an actual release process.
The assistant-only loss masking contribution repeats the first fine-tuning bullet.
items.because: As written, it reads like the same contribution is being claimed twice.

items.says: Clarify the evidence that the model reproduced tool outputs more faithfully.
The diagnostics triage achievement is repeated in an apparently unrelated project.
items.because: It should appear in the section that reflects where the work happened.

items.says: Clarify your contribution to the triage branch launch.
Explain how the backlog reduction was measured.
Specify the workload and memory usage being compared.
items.because: Otherwise, the 4x result is difficult to assess.

items.says: Confirm the memory saving did not materially change model quality or the training setup.
items.because: Otherwise, the 4x result is difficult to assess.

items.says: Clarify the load-test conditions and whether 180 ms was p95 under those conditions.
Confirm the build threshold uses the same workload and measurement process.
Fix the tense inconsistency in the CI sentence.
Explain the three-day release cycle, including its previous duration and what changed.
items.because: That would make the scale of the improvement clear.

items.says: Explain whether you implemented, helped with, or maintained the fleet migration.
Quantify the backlog or dispatch impact if possible.
items.because: Otherwise, the causal link to morning dispatch delays may be challenged.

items.says: Clarify what “Owner” means and whether the suite is a personal, team, or externally used project.
Add a project link.
items.because: It would help readers verify the scope and inspect the implementation.

items.says: Confirm that “Present” matches the submission date.
Replace or substantiate the broad AI-first adoption-and-impact claim with concrete work and evidence.
items.because: It does not give the reader a concrete contribution or verifiable outcome.

items.says: Define what “raw conversation grew 100x” measures.
Explain how the 10K-token limit was tested and under what conditions.
items.because: The result should be reproducible or defensible.

items.says: Explain how the 50-way fan-out test was run.
Explain how you confirmed the failures were resolved, including the failure mode and your fix.
items.because: It is a strong technical claim.

items.says: Clarify your specific contribution as a contributor.
Link the repository and, if available, merged changes or documentation.
items.because: The general code profile alone may not show what you did.

items.says: Identify the eight metrics you integrated.
items.because: “Integrated 8” is difficult to evaluate without knowing what was added.

items.says: Distinguish your implementation from existing framework code.
items.because: It is unclear what you owned.

items.says: Explain what the Kendall correlation compares.
items.because: Without context, the result can sound more conclusive than the test supports.

items.says: Explain how degradation was introduced.
items.because: Without context, the result can sound more conclusive than the test supports.

items.says: Clarify whether the 400+ trials were independent reports or repeated evaluations.
items.because: Without context, the result can sound more conclusive than the test supports.

items.says: The backlog bullet duplicates a company achievement and appears misplaced in the evaluation project.
items.because: It creates a confusing connection between an evaluation framework and an industrial diagnostics system.

items.says: Separate programming languages from tools or workflows.
items.because: That would make the skills section easier to scan.

items.says: Add relevant frameworks, libraries, or methods where you have hands-on evidence.
items.because: The ML & Agents list is very short compared with the experience described.
